title: Business Card
brief: A boutique letterpress studio needs a clean, confident business card that reflects their craft — minimal, typographic, print-ready.
dimensions: 3.5 x 2 in (89 x 51 mm), 0.125 in bleed
requirements: Studio logo or wordmark (type-based is fine)
Bleed extended to edges if using a background color
steps: Create a new document at 3.5 x 2 in with 0.125 in bleed on all sides.
Block out a simple hierarchy: name (largest), title (smaller), contact details (smallest).
Choose one typeface, using weight (not multiple fonts) to create contrast.
If using a background color, extend it fully into the bleed area.
Export a print-ready PDF with marks and bleed included.
checklist: Text fits comfortably within the safe margin
Background color (if any) extends into bleed
Exported as print PDF with bleed marks
commonMistakes: Text placed too close to the trim edge
Forgetting to extend background color to bleed
finalChallenge: Design two variants — one with a colored background, one white — using the exact same type hierarchy, to see how strong your hierarchy really is without relying on color.

title: Event Flyer
brief: Create an A4 promotional flyer announcing a one-day design conference, built to be printed and handed out at partner venues.
dimensions: A4 portrait (210 x 297 mm), 3 mm bleed
requirements: Registration info or QR code placeholder
steps: Set up an A4 document with 3mm bleed.
Establish a 3-level hierarchy: event name, date/location, supporting details.
Place a hero image or bold color block to anchor the top third of the page.
Add a registration call-to-action near the bottom, visually separated from other content.
Preflight and export a print-ready PDF.
checklist: All required info present (name, date, location, speakers, registration)
commonMistakes: Cramming too much text with no breathing room
Weak contrast between the event name and supporting details
finalChallenge: Redesign your flyer for a second event with completely different content, reusing your layout structure and paragraph styles to prove the system holds up.

title: One-Page Poster
brief: A striking single-image poster for a jazz festival, meant to work at a glance from across a room.
dimensions: A3 portrait (297 x 420 mm), 3 mm bleed
requirements: One dominant visual element (image or bold typography)
Festival name as the clear focal point
steps: Set up an A3 document with bleed.
Choose one dominant element — either a large image or oversized type — as the focal point.
Keep supporting text minimal: date, venue, and nothing else.
Use generous whitespace; resist the urge to fill every area.
Export a print-ready PDF.
checklist: Poster reads clearly from a distance
commonMistakes: Adding too much supporting text out of habit
Competing focal points instead of one clear hero element
Small type that won't be legible at poster viewing distance
finalChallenge: Print (or export at 100%) and view your poster from 3 meters away. If the name isn't instantly legible, revise the hierarchy.

title: Restaurant Menu
brief: A single-fold two-panel menu for a neighborhood café, organized into clear sections with prices.
dimensions: A4 landscape, folds to A5, 3 mm bleed
requirements: Paragraph styles for section headers, item names, and descriptions
steps: Set up an A4 landscape document with a 2-column grid (one per panel) and bleed.
Create paragraph styles for: Section Header, Item Name, Item Description, Price.
Use a right-aligned tab stop with a leader (dotted line) to align prices consistently.
Apply styles consistently across every section.
Fold-test by printing at reduced size to confirm panels read correctly.
checklist: All prices align using a tab leader, not spaces
4 distinct paragraph styles created and applied
Sections are visually separated and easy to scan
commonMistakes: Aligning prices with spacebar instead of tabs, causing uneven columns
Not testing how content reads once folded
finalChallenge: Add a seasonal specials section using your existing styles only — no new manual formatting — to prove your style system scales.

title: Tri-Fold Brochure
brief: A print-ready tri-fold brochure promoting a travel package, requiring full preflight and press-ready export.
requirements: 3 folded panels with distinct content per panel
Cover panel, inside spread, back panel
At least 2 images with text wrap
steps: Set up guides marking the 3 fold panels (roughly 99mm each on A4 landscape).
Design a cover panel with the destination name as the focal point.
Design the inside spread with itinerary details, using text wrap around at least one image.
Design the back panel with contact info and a call to action.
Set bleed, run Preflight, and fix all warnings.
Export as PDF/X-4 with marks and bleed for commercial printing.
checklist: Content respects fold lines (no important text crossing a fold)
commonMistakes: Important text or logos sitting exactly on a fold line
Skipping the preflight check before export
Using screen-resolution images pulled from the web
finalChallenge: Fully preflight your file against a custom profile requiring 300 PPI minimum and zero missing fonts, and fix every flagged issue before export.
